page: Microsoft Azure E48ads_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor based on the x86_64 architecture. Managed under Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 48 dedicated vCPUs spanning 24 physical cores running at 3.7 GHz. The hardware configuration incorporates 384.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Storage resources include 2835 GB of local NVMe SSD space alongside support for premium remote storage. The instance operates without discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong compute and memory subsystem performance, placing the instance in the top quartile across multiple standardized tests. It records a Geekbench multi-core score of 20385.0 and a single-core score of 2095.0, supported by hardware-level instructions including AVX-512 (F, VNNI, BF16), AES, and SHA_NI. In data-handling assessments, the system achieved 22302.56 operations in PassMark database benchmarks and 67.13 million operations per second in Redis SET operations. Cached small-block memory reads reach 3648.86 GB/sec, whereas uncached 256 MB sequential reads and writes measure 114.93 GB/sec and 83.19 GB/sec respectively.

The bundled NVMe storage and high memory density provide efficient hardware utilization for workloads requiring local low-latency scratch space or caching without relying on external network-attached volumes. Conversely, executing large machine learning models entirely on CPU cores presents clear throughput limitations, as shown by text generation speeds of 2.59 tokens per second on a 70B parameter model. The configuration is primarily matched to large relational databases, distributed in-memory caches, large software build pipelines, and transactional enterprise systems.
description: Microsoft Azure E48ads_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor with 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores running at 3.7 GHz. The instance delivers 384.0 GB of memory and 2835 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage, providing an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio without attached GPU hardware. Benchmark results place it in the upper quartile for PassMark database operations, Geekbench multi-core execution, and Redis throughput, which reached 67.13 million SET operations per second. Uncached memory bandwidth and large language model generation represent performance tradeoffs compared to specialized accelerator platforms. With dense memory and integrated local NVMe drives, the system minimizes external storage overhead for high-IOPS applications. Azure E48ads_v6 is engineered for in-memory databases, Redis deployments, enterprise software compilation, and high-concurrency transactional database workloads.
